items.title: Mercury 3 makes diffusion models credible
items.oneliner: Mercury 3 claims 1,068 tokens per second and 1M context. Diffusion LLMs just became a real serving option.

items.title: Mistral ships a compact forecasting model
items.oneliner: Mistral's 209M-parameter Timestral beats larger time-series models on public benchmarks. Specialized foundation models are getting brutally efficient.

items.title: MiniMax cuts agent costs sharply
items.oneliner: MiniMax says M3.1 Flash is 3x faster and 70% cheaper. Agent economics are starting to matter more than demos.

items.title: DeepSeek pushes agent pricing lower
items.oneliner: DeepSeek opened Search and Fetch at $0.75 per 1,000 requests. Cheap retrieval is becoming table stakes for agents.

items.title: Plex bugs are already being exploited
items.oneliner: Attackers are chaining recent Plex flaws to drop cryptominers. Unpatched media servers are now easy initial access points.

items.title: Cairn exposes AI cyber operations
items.oneliner: Researchers found 20-plus exposed Cairn panels automating targeting, exploitation, and persistence. Offensive AI ops are already operationally messy and real.

items.title: Let's Encrypt adds more validation viewpoints
items.oneliner: Let's Encrypt is moving to seven validation requests across remote perspectives. BGP hijacks just got harder to turn into bad certificates.

items.title: GitHub Actions had a rough day
items.oneliner: GitHub degraded Actions, Pages, and Webhooks with delayed workflows and builds. Your CI dependency chain is still a single point of pain.

items.title: KiviDB targets Redis with vector search
items.oneliner: KiviDB claims 21 million pipelined GETs per second with Redis compatibility. The memory database layer is fragmenting fast.

items.title: A new profiler explains build bottlenecks
items.oneliner: Buildprof traced Bun compile times and showed LTO choices mattered more than language. Tooling still beats intuition on performance.
